title: Slow PC with disk health warnings
symptom: PC has become very slow and shows warnings about the hard drive's health
user_description: My PC takes ages to open anything now, and this morning a message popped up saying something about the disk and backing up. I have all my spreadsheets on it!

options.text: Back up his data first, then check the drive's health (SMART status in the manufacturer's tool or a SMART checker) and plan a replacement if it is failing
options.why: A drive warning means it may fail soon. Getting the data off comes first, then the health check confirms whether the drive needs replacing.

options.text: Defragment the drive several times to speed it up
options.why: Defragmenting puts heavy load on a drive that may be failing, and does nothing for a hardware fault.

options.text: Ignore the warning, since the PC still works
options.why: Drives that warn about their health can fail without more notice, and the data could be lost.

options.text: Run a disk repair first, before backing anything up
options.why: Repairs can stress a failing drive and sometimes make data harder to recover. Back up first.

hints: What matters most if this drive stops working tomorrow?
Can a drive report its own health?
Will software tweaks fix a worn-out drive?
real_world_tip: SMART is the self-monitoring built into most drives. Treat a health warning as urgent: copy the data off today, then replace the drive.
